description: Files directly in a module's application/ folder (backend.md section 3 rule 3: the last resort for shared application logic). Each entry is '<module>/application/<file>.ts' with a 'reason': the step of rule 3 that was tried and why it did not apply. A new file fails tests/architecture/api/pinned.test.ts until it is recorded here in the same pull request. The Epic aimed for an empty list; the remaining ones are run-lookup-requests, repository-cleanup and the read models shown whole by more than one feature, each with its reason below.

environments/application/preview-compose.reason: Steps 1 to 5 tried: it calls the Repository's source port, so it cannot live in the domain (1); it is a sequence of one read and the judgement of its text, not one infrastructure capability (2); the settings save and the build request both read the Compose file and map its refusals, and handlers never call each other, so no one use case holds it (3); it is no job or event, since the operator waits for the refusals (4); copying the read and the refusal mapping into both would let their wording drift (5).

environments/application/preview-state-r.reason: Steps 1 to 5 tried: it reads the operation repository, the controller presence and the clock, so it cannot live in the domain, which holds the derivation itself in PreviewState (1); it is a sequence of several ports, not one infrastructure capability (2); the get and the save of the Preview settings both show its state, and handlers never call each other, so no one use case holds it (3); it is no job or event (4); copying its steps and the link rule into both would drift (5).

environments/application/preview-view.ts.reason: Steps 1 to 5 tried: a result shape is no behaviour of the entity (1); no infrastructure capability is involved (2); get and save both show the Project's whole Preview, and handlers never call each other, so no one use case holds it (3); it is no job or event (4); copying its fields into both would drift, since a new field must be added to every copy (5). It is a type with a pure mapping from the entity: no rule, no repository or port call.

executions/application/run-lookup-reques.reason: Steps 1 to 5 tried: its steps are one transaction across two aggregates (the Run and its lookup), so they fit on neither one (1); no infrastructure capability is involved (2); the five entry points that request a lookup (refresh, failing checks, review comments, Follow-up refresh, daily refresh) do not share their other steps, so they are not one use case (3); the answer is needed at once, so it cannot be a job or event (4); the steps are too many to repeat (5).

It is a type with a pure mapping from the entity: no rule, no repository or port call.

projects/application/repository-cleanup..reason: Steps 1 to 5 tried: it calls ports (Git, Deploy keys), so it cannot live in the domain (1); it is a sequence of several ports, not one infrastructure capability (2); the operator's Disconnect and the start-up resume differ in trigger and input, so they are not one use case (3); it cannot be a job or event, since the operator's Disconnect answers with the outcome (4); it is too long to repeat: three ordered steps, the record delete and the failure handling (5).

environments/application/preview-build-r.reason: Steps 1 to 5 tried: it reads the Repository's source port, the settings, the controller presence and the Compose judge, so it cannot live in the domain, which holds the refusals and the limit in PreviewState and PreviewStartLimit (1); it is a sequence of several ports, not one infrastructure capability (2); the build route and Reset both prepare and request a build, and handlers never call each other, so no one use case holds it (3); the operator waits for the refusals, so it is no job or event (4); copying its steps into both would let the order of the checks drift (5).
